featured_reviews.name: Daksh Saroha
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place was suggested by a student and I can honestly understand why a young person might be impressed by the place. The place has that bling blang angsty loud music teenager vibe to it. But it's also like this place is managed by said teenager. And that's my biggest qualm.

My friend and I had an appointment for 4pm. We were there at 3:45 expecting to be in and out quickly. How long can a tattoo possibly take when I already have the design finalised? I had another engagement to attend at 7:30. I thought it was a safe margin.

How wrong I was. The manager attended us within the hour. The process started 3 hours later. A process which hardly took 15-20 minutes. I got my tattoos done by 8. Post which they said "now they will do your friend's tattoos". This is at 8pm! We had an appointment at 4!

The artists are fine. They do what they're told. They do a decent enough job. There's not much talking in between because, as some others have pointed out, they're worked like they're in a factory. Minimal breaks. Back to back to back jobs.

It is the management I have a problem with. They know how to take a reservation but they don't know how to keep it. They don't respect people's time. They don't do the one thing they're supposed to. Manage. Reservations mean nothing. People's time has no value.

And maybe that's okay for students and rich people who have nothing better to do with their lives. But some of us have respect for a modicum of punctuality.

And all this to not even mention the complomentary piercing that was offered beforehand. When I asked about it, they simply said better luck next time. Which was the same response when my friend expressed her displeasure (although she was happy that she didn't get a permanent mark on her body by a company this unprofessional).

1.5/5 just for the artist.
Otherwise should be 0.
The entire experience left such a bad taste in my mouth. Can't recommend this one to anyone.
